The image displays several soybean stems and pods. Key features include what appears to be a white, fluffy mycelial growth on one of the stems. Additionally, there are small, black, hard structures visible on and near the infected stems. One is clearly visible on a desiccated leaf or flower part, and more are seen in the crop image on a stem. These structures are consistent in appearance with the sclerotia described for White Mold. The description for White Mold mentions "lesions usually develop first at stem nodes," "infected stems often become soft and watery, covered with white moldy growth," and importantly, "Hard, black sclerotia that resemble rodent droppings develop on or inside infected stems and pods; white fluffy mycelium covers stem lesions under moist conditions." The visual evidence of both white mycelium and black sclerotia strongly points to this diagnosis.
